description: Multi-source conclusion confidence rubric for the Phase 5 conclusion-synthesis pipeline (app/services/conclusion_grader.py). Synthesizes and scores individual claims across both peer-reviewed research papers and official verified online resources (NIH, EFSA, USDA, Health Canada, DailyMed). Four weighted categories sum to a maximum of 100 points, mapped to letter grades A-E.

grade_bands.label: Very high confidence — strong clinical trial consensus fully backed by official health/regulatory agency authorization
High confidence — solid empirical evidence or official monograph authorization with minor research gaps
Moderate confidence — plausible but limited paper evidence; recognized ingredient without explicit health claim authorization
Low confidence — weak study design, inconsistent data, or flagged by authorities for insufficient efficacy evidence
Very low confidence — minimal evidence, contradicted by studies, or flagged with toxicity/safety warnings by official agencies

categories.label: Peer-Reviewed Study Evidence Strength
categories.description: Quality of supporting empirical studies based on paper_grading_rubric.json (study design, sample size, methodology rigor, funding bias). Reflects highest-tier papers supporting the claim.

score_tiers.example: Primarily backed by systematic reviews or high-grade RCTs (Paper Grade A, 85-100)
Backed by solid clinical trials with minor methodology limitations (Paper Grade B, 70-84)
Backed by fair-quality studies, observational human data, or notable cohort limitations (Paper Grade C, 50-69)
Backed by a single borderline paper just above the grading threshold
Paper evidence quality minimal, unverified, or poorly documented

categories.label: Official Regulatory & Health Authority Backing
categories.description: Degree of official health agency authorization, monograph recognition, established RDAs, or approved health claims from official resources (NIH, EFSA, USDA, Health Canada, DailyMed).

score_tiers.example: Explicitly monographed with authorized health claims or established daily reference intake (RDA) by major health authorities (e.g., EFSA, Health Canada, NIH)
Listed in official regulatory databases as an authorized dietary/natural health ingredient with clear safety and dosage guidelines
Documented in official reference databases (e.g., PubChem, USDA nutrient tables) without explicit therapeutic health claim endorsement
Minimal regulatory coverage; agency documents note unverified manufacturer claims or insufficient efficacy data
Flagged with official regulatory prohibitions, safety alerts, or tolerable upper intake violation warnings

categories.label: Multi-Source & Cross-Paper Consensus
categories.description: Consistency of the finding across independent research papers AND official regulatory agency guidelines (alignment vs. contradiction). Re-evaluated dynamically during claim synthesis.

score_tiers.example: Supported by 3+ independent papers with full alignment from official agency guidelines; zero contradicting evidence
Supported by 2-3 papers OR 1 strong paper + official regulatory monograph endorsement; no contradicting findings
Supported by a single paper/source, or supported by multiple sources with one minor contradicting outlier
Mixed evidence — roughly equal balance of contradicting paper studies or official regulatory cautions
Contradicted by primary literature or explicitly refuted by official regulatory statements

categories.label: Claim Specificity & Clinical Actionability
categories.description: How precisely the claim specifies effective dosage ranges, target population, and clinical outcome measures for actionable user guidance.

score_tiers.example: Specific dosage range, target population, and precise clinical outcome measure clearly stated
Effective dosage and outcome stated; population described generally
Partial specificity — dosage OR outcome stated, but missing key operational details
Vague claim with minimal actionability or specific detail
No specific dosage, target population, or measurable outcome provided
